content.text: Everything seems good, then in the FedoraVersions.getVersion(String) it throws a java.io.IOException.
However it does it from something called a
DelegatingMethodAccessorImpl
or a
ResourceMethodInvocationHandlerFactory
These seems to be part of JAX-RS (I think), kinda lost as to how these are called.
Stacktrace of when error occurs is

ResourceMethodInvocationHandlerFactory$1.invoke(Object, Method, Object[]) line: 81	
AbstractJavaResourceMethodDispatcher$1.run() line: 151	
JavaResourceMethodDispatcherProvider$ResponseOutInvoker(AbstractJavaResourceMethodDispatcher).invoke(Object, Object...) line: 171	
JavaResourceMethodDispatcherProvider$ResponseOutInvoker.doDispatch(Object, Request) line: 152	
JavaResourceMethodDispatcherProvider$ResponseOutInvoker(AbstractJavaResourceMethodDispatcher).dispatch(Object, ContainerRequest) line: 104	
ResourceMethodInvoker.invoke(RequestProcessingContext, Object) line: 384	
ResourceMethodInvoker.apply(RequestProcessingContext) line: 342
public javax.ws.rs.core.Response org.fcrepo.http.api.FedoraVersions.getVersion(java.lang.String) throws java.io.IOException
Ok, actually I think the error happens once the response is handed off to JAX-RS. I put a breakpoint here in
FedoraVersions
I can follow it all the way down and back up, but once it returns here (which I assume returns to JAX-RS) then the IOException appears.
does/can JAX-RS call any methods when returning the
Response
? I feel like I am missing a piece of the puzzle.
Ok, forgot that. I was too far in to see it.
Here is the actual error message

org.fcrepo.kernel.api.exception.RepositoryRuntimeException: javax.jcr.ItemNotFoundException: 87a0a8c7505d64676b2b4c-2eb2-4670-919f-5d6397694592
	at org.fcrepo.kernel.modeshape.FedoraResourceImpl.getUnfrozenResource(FedoraResourceImpl.java:731)
	at org.fcrepo.kernel.modeshape.FedoraResourceImpl.getVersionedAncestor(FedoraResourceImpl.java:699)
	at org.fcrepo.http.commons.api.rdf.HttpResourceConverter.getPath(HttpResourceConverter.java:327)
	at org.fcrepo.http.commons.api.rdf.HttpResourceConverter.doBackwardPathOnly(HttpResourceConverter.java:367)
	at org.fcrepo.http.commons.api.rdf.HttpResourceConverter.doBackward(HttpResourceConverter.java:148)
	at org.fcrepo.http.commons.api.rdf.HttpResourceConverter.doBackward(HttpResourceConverter.java:76)
	at com.google.common.base.Converter.correctedDoBackward(Converter.java:164)
	at com.google.common.base.Converter$ReverseConverter.correctedDoForward(Converter.java:244)
	at com.google.common.base.Converter.convert(Converter.java:147)
	at org.fcrepo.kernel.modeshape.rdf.impl.NodeRdfContext.uriFor(NodeRdfContext.java:76)
	at org.fcrepo.kernel.modeshape.rdf.impl.ChildrenRdfContext.lambda$new$50(ChildrenRdfContext.java:63)
	at org.fcrepo.kernel.modeshape.rdf.impl.ChildrenRdfContext$$Lambda$92/1018118789.apply(Unknown Source)
I think this is thrown here (
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/modeshape/FedoraResourceImpl.java#L728-L732)

when we get the triples for the versioned resource, because the version has a child. So it tries to convert the frozen/versioned path to the unfrozen path, but the item is gone so it throws an exception.
I'll do some more digging tomorrow, consider this a bookmark.
And sorry
for dragging you in when I was only half understanding the issue.
Ok, I am not sure how to proceed.
Part of the HttpResourceConverter is to
get the Unfrozen FedoraResource
for any frozen one we encounter.
However in the case of a deleted resource, this returns a
javax.jcr.ItemNotFoundException
This is called because in a normal representation we resolve all the children of the node
here
If you change your request to
curl -i -H"Prefer: return=minimal" http://localhost:8080/rest/collection/fcr:versions/v0
it will complete.
The path of the resource seems to only exist in the actual resource, so deleting any resource makes the path inaccessible.
I tried to replace the RepositoryRuntimeException with the
INACCESSIBLE_RESOURCE
originally created for dealing with restricted paths in Link Headers.
However this causes other errors as it is not
in the domain of the repository
Does this seem like a way to proceed? Generate a fake FedoraResource with a path something like "deletedResource"?

After some discussion on IRC, it seems like this might be caused by a situation in which unversioned contents occur inside versioned containers. If that is correct, then the question arises as to whether we should prevent the situation from occurring to begin with?

could we access a fcr:tombstone from a frozenNode if the actual resource has been deleted? Then we could get the path back to generate the triples in ChildrenRdfContext. I realize that if you delete the tombstone you are back to square one, just trying to see how to resolve this.
, I'm not sure if that would work, but it sounds worth exploring.  If there is a version history, then getting access to it and fulfilling the request sounds great.
If the versions are also deleted (or if the content was never versioned like
suggests), then we should probably return 410 Gone if the parent resource has a tombstone.
, would you mind putting a hold on this ticket until I finish:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1942
I believe they are related and I may have a fix on the way.
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1005
Resolved with
f0db4f2
This bug is seen when a container contains another resource, the container is versioned, the child resource is deleted, then the previously created container version is retrieved.
The following requests demonstrate the error.
curl -i -XPUT localhost:8080/rest/collection
curl -i -XPUT -H"Content-Type: application/pdf" --data-binary @book.pdf localhost:8080/rest/collection/book.pdf
curl -i -XPOST -H"slug: v0" localhost:8080/rest/collection/fcr:versions
curl -i  localhost:8080/rest/collection/fcr:versions/v0
curl -i -XDELETE localhost:8080/rest/collection/book.pdf
curl -i  localhost:8080/rest/collection/fcr:versions/v0
BOOM! 404

Note: In the case where the child resource is a binary, it appears that the binary is not moved to the "fcrepo.binary.directory/trash" when it is deleted, implying that there is still a reference to the binary... which would indicate that the 404 is at the Fedora level, and that Modeshape may still enable restoring the child resource from the container version.
